questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: Whether animals can evolve to cope with climate change
Darwin's life and his long journey around the world
Why the Galapagos Islands have so many colourful birds
How scientists protect animals from dangerous hurricanes
questions.why: Sam says they'll be asking 'can animals evolve to deal with climate change?'

questions.q: According to Kiyoko Gotanda, what did Darwin first think of the finches?
options: He thought they were the most beautiful birds he'd seen
He was surprised by how loudly they sang
He wasn't very interested because they looked dull
He thought they were a kind of parrot
questions.why: She says he 'wasn't that interested' – they were a drab colour and didn't have an interesting song.

questions.q: What did Darwin notice when he looked at the finches back in England?
options: They all had exactly the same shape and size
Their beaks varied from island to island
They had changed colour during the journey
They could only live on one of the islands
questions.why: He looked at variation in beak shape and size, and recalled certain finches were found on certain islands.

questions.q: Which finches were more likely to survive and have babies?
options: Those with the most colourful feathers
Those with the loudest and nicest song
Those that flew to other islands
Those whose beaks got them more food
questions.why: Sam says finches born with a beak that could help them get more food were more likely to survive.

questions.q: What have studies of birds in Brazil and red deer in Scotland shown?
options: Warmer weather has made their bodies smaller
They have grown bigger to survive colder winters
They have moved to new areas to find food
They are not affected by climate change at all
questions.why: Sam says warmer temperatures have caused them to evolve smaller bodies – it's easier to keep cool.

questions.q: What is Thor Hanson trying to find out about anole lizards?
options: Why they have become more colourful
How they find food in the Caribbean forests
How hurricanes are affecting them
Why they are moving to colder islands
questions.why: Rob says he wants to see how hurricanes, an effect of climate change, are affecting the lizards.

options: Those with long back legs and very small toe pads
The largest and heaviest lizards
Those that hid under the ground
Those with strong front legs and big toe pads
questions.why: Large toe pads and strong front legs gave a tighter grip, and smaller back legs reduced the drag.

questions.q: Why does Sam think the lizard changes would have surprised Darwin?
options: The lizards changed colour very quickly
They happened in only about forty years
The lizards did not pass on their traits
They happened only on one small island
questions.why: She says evolution usually takes hundreds of years, but these changes happened in around forty years.
